text:
Carolina arrives with the better numbers almost everywhere. At five on five, CAR has taken 57% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in its games, while VAN sits at 40%. The model projects 3.69 expected goals for CAR tonight against 2.46 for VAN. The two met on Oct 8, and CAR won 7-2 in a game it deserved to win 79% of the time, meaning it took the win in 79% of simulated replays of every shot. The Hurricanes are 4-1-0 in their last five and had more expected goals in all five, including the 3-2 loss at CGY. Vancouver is 0-4-1 over the same stretch with 38% of the expected goals. The Canucks have also lost seven straight (0-6-1), outscored 30-13, and the chances back that up.

Special teams favor CAR. Its power play creates 0.98 expected goals a game, and VAN's penalty kill allows 0.91. CAR does take 4.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays. Marco Rossi could return for VAN, while CAR is without Taylor Hall and Mark Jankowski. In net, projected starters Pyotr Kochetkov (CAR) and Leevi Meriläinen (VAN) are both positive this season in goals saved above expected, which compares actual saves to what an average goalie would make: +3.9 for Kochetkov, +3.3 for Meriläinen. Last season they were -0.03 and -17.93.

For CAR, Andrei Svechnikov has a 40% chance to score and Sebastian Aho has a 77% chance at a point, both flagged as top power-play threats. Jake DeBrusk leads VAN at 25% to score.
